ch2_p5_hitl_sim_solo.text: Welcome to the Human-in-the-Loop Triaging Simulator. Adjust the batch size, automated cost, manual audit cost, and downstream error loss to observe how the mathematically optimal routing threshold dynamically minimizes total acquisition costs while bounding uncorrected risk.

ch2_p5_hitl_sim_duo.text: Let us explore cost-optimal triaging in action! Notice how shifting the error penalty instantly raises the bar for automated ingestion, routing more ambiguous records to human review.

ch2_p5_chk1_solo.text: Time for Active Checkpoint 1. In a medical document ingestion pipeline with automated processing cost of one cent, physician audit cost of three dollars, and billing error loss of one hundred and fifty dollars, what is the exact optimal uncertainty routing threshold?

ch2_p5_chk1_duo.text: Active Checkpoint 1! Remember Dr. Nova's derivation: tau-star equals the ratio of marginal human review cost to uncorrected error loss. What is the exact numerical cutoff?

ch2_p5_chk1_feedback_correct.text: Outstanding! tau-star equals three dollars divided by one hundred and fifty dollars, which yields exactly zero point zero two zero, or two percent. Records with predicted model uncertainty below two percent are safely ingested automatically, while anything above two percent is routed to physician review.

ch2_p5_chk1_feedback_incorrect.text: Not quite. Remember our optimal triaging theorem: tau-star equals C-m divided by L-error. Dividing three dollars by one hundred and fifty dollars gives zero point zero two zero, or two percent. Review the formula and try again.

ch2_p5_kappa_sim_solo.text: Welcome to the Inter-Rater Reliability and Cognitive Fatigue Simulator. Explore how observed and chance agreement govern Fleiss' Kappa, and adjust shift duration to witness the exponential rise in human error predicted by the Weibull hazard model.

ch2_p5_kappa_sim_duo.text: Let us test human rater dynamics! Drag the shift slider past four hours to see how cognitive fatigue causes transcription errors to spike, and test why Fleiss' Kappa requires correcting for random chance.

ch2_p5_chk2_solo.text: Time for Active Checkpoint 2. Three medical annotators categorize one hundred radiology images into normal versus abnormal. The observed pairwise agreement is eighty-five percent, while chance agreement is fifty percent. What is Fleiss' Kappa, and what is its operational interpretation?

ch2_p5_chk2_duo.text: Active Checkpoint 2! Apply the Fleiss' Kappa formula: P-bar minus P-sub-e divided by one minus P-sub-e. What is the calculated value and how should the engineering team interpret it?

ch2_p5_chk2_feedback_correct.text: Spot on! Fleiss' Kappa equals zero point eight five minus zero point five zero, divided by one minus zero point five zero, which gives zero point seven zero. On the Landis and Koch benchmark, a Kappa of zero point seven zero signifies substantial inter-rater reliability, proving the annotation guidelines are robust for production ground-truth generation.

ch2_p5_chk2_feedback_incorrect.text: Incorrect. Make sure to subtract chance agreement from both the numerator and the denominator. Zero point three five divided by zero point five zero equals zero point seven zero, which corresponds to substantial agreement. Review the scale and try again.
